signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Intervention
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.7987, having collapsed through its SMA20/50 cluster at 0.8112/0.8081. The US Treasury’s unexpected decision to double and pull forward bond buybacks has triggered a 'Bessent Put' in the long end, forcing a broad USD liquidation across G10 pairs. CHF 1W average performance is +0.975% vs USD -1.172%, creating a massive 2.146% G10 spread that anchors the current regime. Despite the 375bp nominal carry disadvantage for CHF, the market is prioritizing the policy-driven USD downside as the US Treasury steps into the bond market. This intervention-driven repricing is confirmed by institutional desks at ING and Saxo, who view the move as a signal of willingness to cap US yields. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CHF; USD underperformance dominates carry considerations. Catalyst: next SNB meeting — hold at 0.00% priced. Risk: Treasury buyback effects prove short-lived and the 375bp carry differential reasserts dominance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.73 is trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (159.91/161.03/158.28), marking a significant breakdown in technical structure. The options market is pricing in aggressive downside protection with 25d RR at -2.02, a strong put skew that aligns with a VRP of -1.3%—indicating an unusual supply-side thinness in options protection. While a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage technically supports USD, the correlation with VIX has turned positive (+0.436 vs norm +0.097, z=+1.63σ), signaling that JPY is no longer functioning as a safe haven and is instead tracking volatility-driven carry unwinds. Rising geopolitical tension following Iran's vow to defend national interests against US sanctions introduces fresh volatility that typically favors JPY strength via the carry-unwind mechanism. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; technical breakdown and options skew favor further downside. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting — hike bias priced. Risk: USD/JPY recovers SMA200 at 158.28 and carry demand resumes on yield stabilization.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT vs Retail Divergence + ESI
signals.text: AUD/USD is holding at 0.7124, supported by its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7041/0.6999/0.6948). We observe a significant divergence as retail sentiment hits an 85% short extreme while institutional COT Leveraged Funds remain net long (+45,727). This institutional-retail split occurs as Australia's 10Y yield offers a +40bp premium over the US 10Y, providing a structural carry tailwind for the AUD. However, the AUD ESI at -10.3 reflects a moderate negative bias in domestic data that contradicts the bullish positioning. This combination suggests a 'crowded long' risk if US data continues to surprise to the upside, potentially triggering an institutional unwind against the retail short. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; institutional longs vs retail short extreme creates a standoff. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold at 4.35% priced. Risk: AUD/USD closes below SMA20 (0.7041), signaling institutional capitulation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + Yield Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1686, sustained by a bearish bear steepener regime in the US curve and a -139bp Bund-UST 10Y spread. The pair exhibits an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.3%, with ATM IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.8%, signaling that the options market is paying up for protection ahead of next month's ECB meeting. This hedging demand persists despite a 135bp nominal carry disadvantage for the Euro. ECB holds at 2.4%. Trade bias: Long EUR/USD; hedging demand and policy repricing favor the Euro. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: US CPI surprise re-establishes the 'higher-for-longer' Fed narrative, crushing the current USD liquidation.
